summary: Frontend-only verification of iteration-3 bug fixes (site switching + Maintenance tab). Logged in as admin, exercised both switch orders across all 4 sites, empty-site task dialog, full task CRUD + complete flow, stale-data regression on Pannes/Stock/Analyses/Equipements/Dashboard, and one tech-vs-admin scope spot-check. ZERO pageerror / Uncaught / console errors observed (only expected 403 network log lines from the deliberate scope probe). All 5 requested items PASS.

issues: 'Prochaine échéance' uses the native browser date input (renders as 08/29/2026 US format) instead of the shadcn Calendar/Popover — inconsistent with FR locale used elsewhere (list shows '28 sept. 2026')

action_items: Optional: replace native <input type=date> in Maintenance dialog with shadcn Calendar for FR date format consistency
Optional: completing a task sets next_due = done_at + frequency (Aug 29 + 15 = Sep 13) rather than previous_due + frequency (Aug 30 + 15 = Sep 14). Confirm intended business rule.

Optional: deleting a maintenance task leaves its maintenance-history entries behind (one residual 'Digesteur principal' intervention on Bournezeau from this QA run); consider cascade or keep intentionally as audit trail.
critical_code_review_comments: Maintenance.jsx load()/reset pattern is correct: state reset happens synchronously in the effect before the async fetch, so no stale flicker; verified by polling task rows every 500ms after a switch.

load() is called twice on mount in dev (React StrictMode double effect) — harmless but doubles GETs; consider an AbortController to also guard against out-of-order responses if a user switches sites rapidly (not reproducible manually, but the current code has no request-cancellation/ordering guard).

Verified: switch-then-nav and nav-then-switch to /maintenance both clean; empty site shows no-equip-warning + disabled save-task; DialogDescription present; create/complete/delete flow works with 'Intervention enregistrée' toast; tech sees only Bournezeau and gets 403 'Site non autorisé' on GET/POST for another site.
rca_of_the_issue: Original user complaint could not be reproduced as a crash. The three defensive fixes (state reset on siteId change, try/catch + Sonner toast around the 3 parallel GETs, and amber warning + disabled save on 0-equipment sites) all behave as designed and eliminate the perceived empty/stale states. Only residual risk: no request cancellation on rapid consecutive site switches (out-of-order responses could still land), which was not reproducible at human interaction speed.
